G0554:
ἀπ-εκ-δύω
to strip off clothes or arms; mid., to strip off from oneself: Col.3:9; to strip, despoil (mid, for act., ICC, in l; but cf. Lft., Ellic.), Col.2:15.†
G3561:
νεομηνία (Att.. contr., νουμ-, Rec.), -ας, ἡ
(νέος, μήν), [in LXX chiefly for חֹדֶשׁ ;]
new moon: of the Jewish festival, Col.2:16.†
G2603:
κατα-βραβεύω
(βραβεύς, an umpire, cf βραβεῖον)
to give judg­ment against, condemn (see Field, Notes, 196; Abbott, Essays, 104 f.): Col.2:18.†
G1687:
ἐμβατεύω
[in LXX: with accusative, Jos.19:49 (נָחַל, Jos.19:51 (חָלַק pi.); before εἰς, 1Ma.12:25 1Mac 13:20 1Mac 14:31 1Mac 15:40; metaphorically, 2Ma.2:30 * ;] (ἐμβάτης ἐμβαίνω)
1. to step in or on (Soph.), hence
(a) to frequent, haunt, dwell in (Æsch., Eur.); metaphorically, Col.2:18 (dwelling in, R, txt.; taking, R, mg.);
(b) to invade (1Mac, ll with; metaphorically, Col, Lc.).
2. to enter on, come into possession of (Eur., Dem.; LXX, Jos, H. with); on the difficulties of reading and interpretation in this passage, see Lft, Col., 194 f., 252; ICC, 268 ff.; Field, Notes, 197; Milligan, NTD, 177; and for exx. from π., MM, Exp., xii (cf. κενεμβ.).†
G1379:
δογματίζω
[in LXX: Est.3:9 (כָּתַב ni.), Dan LXX 2:13, 15 (דָּת), I Est.6:34, 2Ma.10:3 2Mac 15:36, 3Ma.4:11 * ;]
to decree. Mid., to subject oneself to an ordinance: Col.2:20.†
G2345:
θιγγάνω
[in LXX for נָגַע, Exo.19:12 * ;]
1. to touch, handle: Col.2:21, Heb.12:20" (LXX) .
2. to injure (like Heb. נָגַע, and as in Eur., Iph. Aul., 1351): with genitive, Heb.11:28.†
SYN.: see: ἅπτω
G0671:
ἀπό-χρησις, -εως, ἡ
(ἀποχράομαι, to use to the full, abuse)
abuse, misuse: Col.2:22 (MM, see word).†
G1479:
ἐθελο-θρησκία (Rec. -εία), -ας, ἡ,
self-imposed worship: Col.2:23 (eccl.; cf. DB, iv, 923a; Cremer, 733).†
G0857:
ἀφειδία (L, -εία), -ας, ἡ
(ἀφειδής, unsparing);
1. extravagance.
2. unsparing treatment, severity: Col.2:23.†
G4140:
πλησμονή, -ῆς, ἡ
(πίμπλημι), [in LXX chiefly for שָׂבֵעַ and cognate forms ;]
a filling up, satiety: πρὸς π. σαρκός (RV, against the indulgence of the flesh; but ICC, in l, for the full satisfaction of the flesh, op. cit., 276 ff.), Col.2:23.†
G0148:
αἰσχρολογία, -ας, ἡ
(αἰσχρός, λέγω),
abusive language, abuse (Lft., ICC, in l.; MM, VGT, see word): Col.3:8.†
G4658:
Σκύθης, -ου, ὁ
Scythian, an inhabitant of Scythia, i.e. Russia and Siberia, a synonym with the Greeks for the wildest of barbarians: Col.3:11.†
G3437:
μομφή, ῆς, ἡ
(μέμφομαι),
poët. form of μέμψις,
blame, com­plaint: Col.3:13.†
G5047:
τελειότης, -ητος, ἡ
(τέλειος), [in LXX: Jdg.9:16, 19 (תָּמִים), Pro.11:3 (תֻּמָּה), Wis.6:15 12:17, Jer.2:2 * ;]
perfection, completeness: Col.3:14, Heb.6:1
G1018:
βραβεύω
(βραβεύς, an umpire), [in LXX: Wis.10:12 * ;]
(a) prop., to act as umpire; hence,
(b) generally, to arbitrate, decide (Isocr., Dem.; Lft., Col., l.with; MM, see word): Col.3:15;
(with) in some late writers, to direct, rule, control (so in Col., l.with, accusative to Thayer, see word, Meyer, in l.), (cf. κατα-βραβεύω).
†
G2170:
εὐχάριστος, -ον
(εὖ, χαρίζομαι), [in LXX for חֵן, Pro.11:16 * ;]
1. = εὔχαρις, winning, gracious, agreeable (Pr, l.with).
2. grateful, thankful: Col.3:15.†
G4087:
πικραίνω
(πικρός), [in LXX for מָרַד, קָצַף, etc. ;]
to make bitter: Rev.10:9; pass., Rev.8:11 10:10; metaphorically, to embitter (LXX) : pass., before πρός, Col.3:19.†
G0120:
ἀθυμέω, -ῶ (ἄ-θυμος, without heart),
[in LXX for חרה, etc. ;]
to be disheartened: Col.3:21.†
G0469:
ἀντ-από-δοσις, -εως, ἡ
(see supr.), [in LXX chiefly for גְּמוּל, שִׁלּוּם ;]
recompense: Col.3:24 (MM, VGT, see word).†
G3682:
Ὀνήσιμος, -ου, ὁ
(i.e. profitable, ὄνησις, profit),
Onesimus: Col.4:9, Phm 10 (a common name among slaves; see MM, iii, xviii).†
G0431:
ἀνεψιός, -οῦ, ὁ
(cf. Lat. nepos), [in LXX: Num.36:11 ( בֵּן דּוֹד), Tob.7:2 9:6 א * ;]
a cousin: Col.4:10 (MM, VGT, see word).†
G3931:
παρηγορία, -ας, ἡ
(παρηγορέω, to address, exhort, console) [in LXX: 4Ma.5:12 4Mac 6:1 * ;]
1. an address, exhortation (LXX, ll. with).
2. comfort, consolation: Col.4:11.†
G4192:
πόνος, -ου, ὁ
[in LXX for עָמָל, etc. ;]
1. labour, toil: Col.4:13
2. The consequence of toil, distress, suffering, pain (Xen., al., LXX): Rev.16:10-11 21:4.†
SYN.: see: κόπος
G2404:
Ἱεράπολις (WH, Ἱερὰ Πόλις), -εως, ἡ
Hierapolis: a city in the Lyons valley in the Province of Asia: Col.4:13.†
G3065:
Λουκᾶς, -ᾶ, ὁ
(prob. an abbreviation of Λουκανός; see Lft., Col., 240; ICC, Lk., xviii; Bl., § 29; accusative to Ramsay, Exp., Dec., 1912, pp. 502 ff., a by-form of Λούκιος, from Lat. Lucius),
Luke: Lk, tit., Col.4:14, 2Ti.4:11, Phm 24.†
G1214:
Δημᾶς, ὁ
(perh. contracted from Δημήτριος),
Demas, a companion of St. Paul: Col.4:14, Phm 24, 2Ti.4:10.†
G3564:
Νυμφᾶς, -ᾶ, ὁ (WH, R, mg., Νύμφα, which see),
Nymphas: Col.4:15, R, txt. (cf. ICC, Lft., in l).†
Νύμφα (Rec., R, txt., Νυμφᾶς, which see), -ης, ἡ, Nympha (see M, Pr., 48): Col.4:15, WH, R, mg.†
G1837:
ἐξ-ηχέω, -ῶ
[in LXX: Jol.3:14 (הָמוֹן), Sir.40:13, 3Ma.3:2 * ;]
to sound forth (as a trumpet, or thunder; see M, Th., l.with): pass., 1Th.1:8.†
G0362:
ἀνα-μένω
[in LXX for קָוָה pi. ;]
to await "one whose coming is expected, perhaps with the added idea of patience and confidence" with accusative, 1Th.1:10 (see M, Th., in l; MM, VGT, see word).†
G4310: to suffer first or beforehand , (Herdotus Historicus), etc.: to be ill-treated before , ὑπό τινος (Thucydides):—;also, ἀγαθὸν πρ. (Xenophon Historicus) (ML)
G2261:
ἤπιος, -α, -ον
mild, gentle: 1Th.2:7 (WH, R, mg., νήπιος); before πρός, 2Ti.2:24.†
G5162:
τροφός, -oῦ, ἡ
(τρέφω), [in LXX: Gen.35:8, 4Ki.11:2, 2Ch.22:11 Isa.49:23 (יָנַק) * ;]
a nurse: 1Th.2:7.†
G20833:
ὀμείρομαι
(Rec. ὁμ-, see WH, App., 151), = cl. ἱμείρομαι (but prob. with different derivation, see Bl., § 6, 4; Zorell, see word) [in LXX: Job.3:21 (חָכָה)* ;]
to desire earnestly, yearn after: 1Th.2:3.†
G3743:
ὁσίως
(ὅσιος),
adv., [in LXX: 3Ki.8:61, Wis.6:10 * ;]
piously, holily: ὁ. καὶ δικαίως κ. ἀμέμπτως (on the distinction here between these synonyms, see M, Th., 24 f.), 1Th.2:10.†
G0274:
ἀ-μέμπτως,
adv. (ἄμεμπτος), [in LXX: Est.3:13 * ;]
blamelessly (Lft., Notes, 28, 89; MM, VGT, see word -ος): 1Th.2:10 3:13 WH mg., 5:23.†
G4853:
συμ-φυλέτης, -ου, ὁ
(σύν, φυλή; cf. σύμφυλος, Aq.: Zec.13:7; and see Rutherford, NPhr., 255 f.)
a fellow-tribesman, fellow-countryman: 1Th.2:14 (see M, Th., in l, and Intr. liii). Not found elsewhere.†
G1559:
ἐκ-διώκω
[in LXX for בָּרַח hi., צָמַת, הָדַף, etc. ;]
to chase away, drive out: 1Th.2:15 (cf. Deu.6:19, Jol.2:20).†
G0642:
ἀπ-ορφανίζω
(ἀπό, ὀρφανός),
to be bereaved (prop., of a parent, Lft., Notes, 36); metaphorically, 1Th.2:17 (where Field thinks it = χωρισθέντες, Notes, 199).†
G4525:
σαίνω
1. prop. (Hom., al.), of dogs, to wag the tail, fawn.
2. Metaphorical, of persons, with accusative, to fawn upon, flatter, beguile: pass., 1Th.3:3 (for conjectural emendations of the text, see ICC, and M, Th., in l).†
G5105:
τοι-γαρ-οῦν
an inferential particle, [in LXX: Job.22:10 24:22, Sir.41:16, al. ;]
wherefore then, so therefore: 1Th.4:8, Heb.12:1 (Hat., Plat., al.).†
G2312:
θεο-δίδακτος, -ον
taught of God (cf. διδακτοὶ θεοῦ, Jhn.6:45): 1Th.4:9.†
G4035:
περι-λείπομαι depon. mid, and pass.,
[in LXX: 2Ch.34:21 A (שָׁאַר ni.), 2Ma.1:31 2Mac 8:14, 4Ma.12:6 4Mac 13:18 * ;]
to be left remaining, remain over, survive: 1Th.4:15 4:17†
G2752:
κέλευσμα, -τος, τό
(κελεύω), [in LXX: Pro.30:27 * ;]
a call, summons, shout of command: 1Th.4:16 (see M, Th., in l).†
G0743:
ἀρχ-άγγελος, -ου, ὁ
(ἄρχι-, ἄγγελος),
archangel, a chief angel: 1Th.4:16, Ju 9 (Cremer, 24; MM, see word).†
G3525:
νήφω
to be sober, abstain from wine; metaphorically, of moral alertness, to be sober, calm, circumspect: 1Th.5:6 5:8, 2Ti.4:5 (see Ellic., in l), 1Pe.1:13 4:7 5:8 (cf. ἐκ-, ἐκ-νήφω, and see MM, xvii).†
SYN.: ἀγρυπνέω, γρηγορέω
G0813:
ἀ-τακτος, -ον
(τάσσω), [in LXX: 3Ma.1:19 * ;]
out of order, out of place (Lat. inordinatus), frequently of soldiers not keeping the ranks, or an army in disarray (cf. 3Ma.1:19); hence, metaphorically, irregular, disorderly (see previous word): 1Th.5:14.†
G3651:
ὁλοτελής, -ές
(ὅλος, τίλος),
complete, perfect.. 1Th.5:23.†
SYN.: ὁλόκληρος (which see), τέλειος. "As regards meaning, ὁλόκληρος can hardly be distinguished from ὁλοτελής though, in accordance with its derivation, it draws more special attention to the several parts to which the wholeness spoken of extends, no part being wanting or lacking in completeness" (M, Th., 78)
G3648:
ὁλό-κληρος, -ον
(ὅλος, κλῆρος, i.e. with all that has fallen by lot), [in LXX: Lev.23:15, Eze.15:5 (תָּמִים), Deu.27:6, Jos.8:31 (9:2) (שָׁלֵם), Zec.11:16 (נָצַב ni.), Wis.15:3, 1Ma.4:47, 4Ma.15:17 * ;]
complete, entire; in NT in ethical sense (as Wis, 4Mac, ll. with), 1Th.5:23; ὁ. καὶ τέλειοι, Jas.1:4.†
SYN.: ὁλοτελής (which see), τελειος (Tr., Syn., § xxii)
G7013:
ἐν-καυκάομαι
(Rec. ἐγκ-, see: ἐν), -ῶμαι [in LXX: 51(52):1 96(97):7 (הָלַל hithp.); Ps 73(74):4 (שָׁאַג); Ps 105(106):47 (שָׁבַח)* ;]
to take pride in, glory in: before ἐν, 2Th.1:4.†
G1730:
ἔν-δειγμα, -τος
(ἐνδείκνυμι),
a plain token, proof: 2Th.1:5 (cf. ἔνδειξις, which refers rather to the "act of proving"; ἔ., with the passive formation, to the thing proved, see Lft., Notes, 100; M, Th., l.with).†
SYN.: τεκμήριον
G5099:
τίνω
[in LXX: Pro.27:12 (τ. ζημίαν, for עָנַשׁ ni.), etc. ;]
to pay: t. δίκην (cf. Pr, l.with), to pay penalty, 2Th.1:9 (see M, Th., in l).†
G1740:
ἐν-δοξάζω
[in LXX for כָּבַד ni., Exo.14:4, 17-18, Eze.28:22, etc.; for עָרַץ, Psa.89:7; Sir.38:6, al. ;]
to glorify: pass., 2Th.1:10-12.†
G1997:
ἐπι-συν-αγωγή, -ῆς, ἡ
(ἐπισυνάγω), [in LXX: 2Ma.2:7 * ;]
a gathering together, assembly: Heb.10:25; before ἐπί, 2Th.2:1 (cf. 2Mac, l.with).†
G2015:
ἐπιφάνεια, -ας, ἡ
(ἐπιφανής), [in LXX: 2Ki.7:23 (יָרֵא), Est.5:1, Amo.5:22, 2Ma.2:21 2Mac 3:24 2Mac 5:4 2Mac 12:22 2Mac 14:16 2Mac 15:27, 3Ma.2:9 3Mac 5:8 3Mac 5:51,* ;] (in late Gk. and Inscr., frequently of deities, see MM, Exp., xiv)
a manifestation, appear­ance: 2Th.2:8, 1Ti.6:14, 2Ti.1:10 4:1 4:8, Tit.2:13 (cf. M, Th., 148 f.).†
G3401:
μιμέομαι, -οῦμαι
(μῖμος, a mimic, an actor), [in LXX: Psa.31:6, Wis.4:2 15:9, 4Ma.9:23 4Mac 9:13 : * ;]
to imitate: 2Th.3:7 3:9 Heb.13:7, 3Jn.11.†
G0812:
ἀτακτέω -ῶ
(ἄτακτος),
primarily, of soldiers marching, to be out of order, to quit the ranks; hence, metaphorically, to be remiss, fail in the performance of duty (in π., of truancy on the part of an apprentice): 2Th.3:7 (on ἀ. and its cognates, see M, Th., 152 ff.; MM, s.vv.).†
G4020:
περι-εργάζομαι
[in LXX: Wis.8:5 א1, Sir.3:23 * ;]
1. to waste one's labour about a thing.
2. to be a busybody: 2Th.3:11 (cf. Plat., Apol., 19 B).†
G2569:
καλο-ποιέω, -ῶ
[in LXX: Lev.5:4 F (καλῶς π., B) * ;]
to do well, act honourably: 2Th.3:13 (cf. Gal.6:9 τὸ καλὸν π.).†
G4593:
σημειόω, -ῶ
(σημεῖον), [in LXX: Psa.4:6 (נָשָׂא)* ;]
to mark, note. Mid., to note for oneself: 2Th.3:14 (frequently in π.; see ICC, M, Th., in l).†
G2085:
ἑτεροδιδασκαλέω, -ῶ
to teach other or different doctrine: 1Ti.1:3 6:3 (cf. CGT, in l; Milligan, NTD, 102).†
G3454:
μῦθος, -ου, ὁ
[in LXX: Wis.17:4 A, Sir.20:19 * ;]
1. speech, con­versation.
2. (a) a story, narrative (Hom.);
(b) later, opposite to λόγος (a true narrative) = Lat. fabula, a myth, fable, fiction: 1Ti.1:4 4:7, 2Ti.4:4, Tit.1:14, 2Pe.1:16.†
SYN.. λόγος, q.v
G1076:
γενεαλογία, -ας, ἡ (see previous word);
1. the making of a pedigree.
2. a genealogy: pl., 1Ti.1:4, Tit.3:9 (see CGT, in l., and ib. Intr., xlix ff.; DB, ii, p. 141).
†
G0562:
ἀπέραντος, -ον
(περαίνω, to complete, finish) [in LXX: Job.36:26 (חֵקֶר אַיִן) 3Mac.20 * ;]
endless, interminable: 1Ti.1:4.†
G0795:
ἀστοχέω, -ῶ
(στόχος, a mark), [in LXX: Sir.7:19 8:9 * ;]
to miss the mark, fail: with genitive, 1Ti.1:6 (so in π., MM, see word); before περί, 1Ti.6:21, 2Ti.2:18.†
G1624:
ἐκ-τρέπω
[in LXX for הָפַךְ, Amo.5:8 * ;]
to turn out of the course, turn aside, with accusative Pass., with middle sense, intrans., to turn aside: Heb.12:13 (R, txt., for be put out of joint, R, mg., see Thayer, see word Westc., in l); figuratively, before εἰς, 1Ti.1:6; ἐπί, 2Ti.4:4; ὀπίσω, 1Ti.5:15; with accusative, to shun, avoid: 1Ti.6:20.†
G1226:
δια-βεβαιόομαι, -οῦμαι
to affirm confidently: Tit.3:8; before περί, 1Ti.1:7 (Cremer, 140).†
G3545:
νομίμως
adv. (νόμιμος, conformable to law), [in LXX: 4Ma.6:18 * ;]
rightly, lawfully: 1Ti.1:8, 2Ti.2:5.†
G0506:
ἀνυπότακτος, -ον
(ά- neg., ὑποτάσσω) [in Sm.: 1Ki.2:12 10:27 (for LXX, λοιμός, בֵּן בְּלִיַּעַל)* ;]
of things, not subject to rule: Heb.2:8; of persons, unruly: 1Ti.1:9, Tit.1:6, 10 (MM, VGT, see word).†
G0462:
ἀν-όσιος, -ον
(ἀ- neg., ὅσιος), [in LXX: Eze.22:9 (זִמָּה, Wis.12:4, 2Ma.7:34 2Mac 8:32, 3Ma.2:2 3Mac 5:7, 4Ma.12:11 * ;]
unholy, profane (Cremer, 464): 1Ti.1:9, 2Ti.3:2 (MM, VGT, see word).†
G0952:
βέβηλος, -ον
(βαίνω, whence βηλός, a threshold), [in LXX chiefly for חֹל ;]
1. permitted to be trodden, accessible (see DCG, ii, 422b); hence,
2. (opposite to ἱερός) unhallowed, profane: of things, 1Ti.4:7 6:20, 2Ti.2:16; of men, 1Ti.1:9, Heb.12:16 (cf. κοινός; Cremer, 140).
†
G3964:
πατρολῴας (-αλῴας, Rec.; in cl. -αλοίας, see Bl., § 3, 3; 6, 2, and cf. μητρολῴας), -ου, ὁ
(πατήρ + ἀλοιάω, to smite),
(a) a parricide: 1Ti.1:9 (Av, R, txt.);
(b) a smiter of his father : ib. (R, mg.).†
G3389:
μητρολῴας (Rec. -αλῴας, in cl., -αλοίας, see B1., § 3, 3; 6, 2), -ου, ὁ
(μήτρρ + ἀλοιάω, to smite)
(a) a matricide: 1Ti.1:9 (AV, R, txt., but see infr.);
(b) a smiter of his mother: 1Ti.1:9 (R, mg., cf. Exo.21:15, and see Ellic., CGT, in l).†
G0409:
ἀνδρο-φόνος, -ου, ὁ
[in LXX: 2Ma.9:28 * ;]
a man-slayer: 1Ti.1:9 (cf. φονεύς, and see MM, VGT, see word).†
G0405:
ἀνδραποδιστής, -οῦ, ὁ
(ἀνδράποδον, a slave, captured in war)
a slave-dealer, kidnapper: 1Ti.1:10 (see MM, VGT, see word).†
G1965:
ἐπί-ορκος, -ον
[in LXX: Zec.5:3 (שָׁבַע ni.) * ;]
1. of oaths, sworn falsely.
2. Of persons, perjured; as subst., a perjurer, false swearer: 1Ti.1:10.†
G5250:
ὑπερ-πλεονάζω
to abound exceedingly: 1Ti.1:14 (Ps Sol 5:19; Herm., Mand., v, 2, 5).†
G0594:
ἀπο-δοχή, -ῆς, ἡ
(ἀποδέχομαι),
acceptance, approbation (Field, Notes, 203): 1Ti.1:15 4:9 (Cremer, 686; MM, see word).†
G5296:
ὑπο-τύπωσις, -εως, ἡ
(ὑποτυπόω, to delineate),
an outline, sketch. Metaphorical, a pattern, example: 1Ti.1:16, 2Ti.1:13.†
SYN.: ὁμοίωμα, τύπος, ὑπόδειγμα (see DB, iii, 696b)
G1783:
ἐν-τευξις, -εως, ἡ
(ἐντυγχάνω, which see), [in LXX: 2Ma.4:3 * ;]
1. a lighting upon, meeting with.
2. conversation.
3. a petition (in this sense common in π.; cf. Deiss., BS, 121 f., 146; MM, Exp., iii): 1Ti.4:5; p1., 1Ti.2:1.†
SYN.: δέησις (which see)
G2263:
ἤρεμος-ον
[in LXX Est.3:13 A* ;]
quiet, tranquil (Luc., al.): 1Ti.2:2.†
SYN: ἡσύχιος, q.v
G2272:
ἡσύχιος, -α, -ον
(= the more frequently ἥσυχος; cf. Wis.18:14, Sir.25:20), [in LXX: Isa.66:2 (רוּחַ נָכֶה)* ;]
quiet, tranquil: 1Ti.2:2, 1Pe.3:4.†
SYN.: ἤρεμος, of tranquillity arising from without; ἡ., from within (see Ellic. on 1Ti, l.with; but also see CGT, ib.).†
G1236:
δι-άγω
[in LXX for עבר hi., etc. ;]
1. to carry over.
2. Of time, to pass: βίον, 1Ti.2:2; absol., to live, before ἐν, Tit.3:3.†
G4587:
σεμνότης, -ητος, ἡ
(σεμνός), [in LXX: 2Ma.3:12 * ;]
gravity: 1Ti.2:2 3:4 (Vg. eastitas, cf. Soph., Lex., and Zorell, see word), Tit.2:7.†
G0487:
ἀντί-λυτρον, -ου, τό
[in Al.: Psa.49:9 * ;]

G0001:
Α, α, ἄλφα (which see), τό, indecl.,
alpha, the first letter of the Greek alphabet. As a numeral, ά = 1, α = 1000. As a prefix, it appears to have at least two and perhaps three distinct senses:
1. ἀ- (before a vowel, ἀν-) negative, as in ἄ-γνωστος, ἄ-δικος.
2. ἀ-, ἁ- copulative, indicating community and fellowship, as in ἁ-πλοῦς, ἀ-κολουθέω, ἀ-δελφός.
3. An intensive force (LS, s. α), as in ἀ-τενίζω is sometimes assumed (but see Boisacq, see word).

insolent luxury, wantonness: Rev.18:3 (a late word, first found in a Comic poet, B.C. 300, see Kennedy, Sources, 41, cf. στρηνιάω).†
G4763:
στρηνιάω, ῶ
(στρῆνος, which see), [in Sm.: Isa.61:6 (אָכַל) * ;]
a word which first appears in the middle comedy (Rutherford, NPhr., 475 f.), to run riot, wax wanton: Rev.18:7-9 (cf. κατα-στρηνιάω).†
SYN.: σπαταλάω (which see), τρυφάω
G1039:
βύσσινος, -η, -ον
(βύσσος), [in LXX chiefly for שֵׁשׁ, בּוּץ, etc. ;]
made of βύσσος, fine linen: Rev.18:12, 16 19:8, 14.†
G4596:
σιρικός (by assimilation of vowels, for σηρικός; see Mayser, 150; WH, Notes, 151), -ή, -όν
(οἱ Σῆρες, a people of India from whom the ancients got the first silk),
silk, silken; as subst., τὸ σ., silken fabric, silk: Rev.18:12 (cf. FlJ, B.J., vii, 5, 4).†
G2367:
θύινος (usually θύϊνος, as Rec.), -η, -ον
(θυία, θύα, an African aromatic tree, with ornamentally veined wood of varying colour, = Lat. citrinus), [in Sm.: 3Ki.10:11 (אַלְמֻגִּים)* ;]
thyme: ξύλον, Rev.18:12 (Diosc.).†
G1661:
ἐλεφάντινος, -η, -ον
(ἐλέφας, ivory), [in LXX for שֵׁן ;]
of ivory: Rev.18:12.†
G4604:
σίδηρος, -ου, ὁ
[in LXX chiefly for בַּרְזֶל ;]
iron: Rev.18:12.†
G3139:
μάρμαρος, -ου, ὁ
(μαρμαίρω, to glisten), [in LXX: Ep. Jer.7:2 * ;]
1. any crystalline stone (Hom., Eur., al.).
2. In later writers, marble: Rev.18:12.†
G2792:
κιννάμωμον(Rec. κινάμ-), -υο, τό
(from the Phænician, see LS, see word, and cf. Heb. קִנָּמוֹן)
cinnamon: Rev.18:13.†
G6007:
ἄμωμον, -ου, τό,
amomum, a fragrant plant of India (RV, spice): Rev.18:13
G4585:
σεμίδαλις, -εως, ἡ
[in LXX chiefly for סֹלֶת ;]
fine wheaten flour: Rev.18:13.†
G4480:
ῥέδη (see WH, App., 151), -ης, ἡ
(a Gallic word),
a chariot: Rev.18:13.†
G3703:
ὀπώρα, -ας, ἡ
[in LXX: Jer.48:32 40:10, 12 (קַיִץ) * ;]
1. late summer, early autumn (the time between the risings of Sirius and Arcturus, i.e. late July, all August and early September).
2. By meton. (as being fruit-time), ripe fruits Rev.18:14 (cf. φθινοπωρινά, Ju 12).†
G3045:
λιπαρός, -ά, -όν
(λίπος, fat), [in LXX: Jdg.3:29, Neh.9:35, Is 30:23 (שָׁמֵן)* ;]
oily, fatty; metaphorically, of living, rich, dainty: τὰ λ. καὶ τ. λαμπρά, Rev.18:14.†
G5094:
τιμιότης, -ητος, ἡ
(τίμιος),
preciousness, worth: Rev.18:19 (cf. Hort on τιμή, 1Pe.2:7).†
G6061:
μύλινος, -η, -ον
(μύλος),
1. made of mill-stone (C.l. 3371)
2. = μυλικός: Rev.18:21 (μύλον, T).†
G3731:
ὅρμημα, -τος, τό
(ὁρμάω) [in LXX: Hos.5:10, Amo.1:11 (עֶבְרָה), etc. ;]
a rush: Rev.18:21.†
G3451:
μουσικός, -ή, -όν
[in LXX: Gen.31:27, Eze.26:13 (שִׁיר), Dan LXX TH Dan.3:5 ff. (זְמָר), Sir.22:6, al. ;]
skilled in the arts, esp. in music; as subst., ὁ μ., a minstrel, musician: Rev.18:22.†
G4538:
σαλπιστής
(so Inscr. and late writers for Mt. σαλπιγκτής), οῦ, ὁ,
a trumpeter: Rev.18:22.†
G0239:
ἁλληλουιά
(Rec. ἀλληλούϊα; Heb. הָלַל יָהּ, praise the Lord), [in LXX in the titles of certain Psa (104 (105), al.), and at the end of Psa.150:1-6; also Tob.13:18, 3Ma.7:13 ;]
hallelujah, alleluia: Rev.19:1, 3-4 19:6.†
G3382:
μηρός, -oῦ, ὁ
[in LXX chiefly for יָרֵךְ ;]
the thigh: Rev.19:16.†
G3990:
πελεκίζω
(πέλεκυς, a battle-axe),
to out off with an axe, esp. to behead: with accusative, Rev.20:4 (Polyb., al.).†
G1136:
Γώγ, ὁ (Heb. גּוֹג), indecl.,
Gog, assoc. with Magog (q.v): Rev.20:8.†
G3098:
Μαγώγ, ὁ indecl. (Heb. מָגוֹג, Gen.10:2, Exo.38:2, al.),
Magog, associated with Gog: Rev.20:8 (see Swete, in l).†
G6059:
κυκλεύω
(κύκλος), [in LXX: 4Ki.3:25 B (סָבַב) * ;]
1. to make a circle, go round.
2. to encircle, surround: with accusative of person(s), Jhn.10:24 (Tr., WH, mg.); with accusative of thing(s), Rev.20:9.†
G2929:
κρυσταλλίζω
(κρύσταλλος),
to shine like crystal, be crystal-clear: Rev.21:11 (ἅπ, λεγ.).†
G5068:
τετράγωνος, -ον
(τετρα-, see supr., + γωνία), [in LXX for רָבַע and cogn. forms ;]
square: Rev.21:16 (Hdt., Plat., al.).†
G1739:
ἐν-δώμησις (Rec. -δόμησις), -εως, ἡ
(δωμάω, to build),
a build­ing in: ἡ ἐ. τ. τείχους αὐτῆς ἴασπις, its wall had jasper built into it, Rev.21:18 (see MM, Exp., xiii; Swete, Ap., l.with).†
G5194:
ὕαλος, -ου, ὁ
[in LXX: Job.28:17 (זְכוּכִית) * ;]
1. (Hdt.) a clear transparent stone.
2. (from Plat. on) glass: Rev.21:18, 21.†
G4552:
σάπφειρος, -ου, ἡ
[in LXX for סַפִּיר ;]
sapphire (perh. = lapis lazuli): Rev.21:19.†
G5472:
χαλκηδών, -όνος, ὁ
chalcedony, "supposed to denote a green silicate of copper found in the mines near Chalcedon " (Swete): Rev.21:19.†
G4665:
σμάραγδος, -ου, ἡ
(and in late writers also ὁ), [in LXX: Exo.28:9 (שֹׁהַם) Exo.36:17 (Exo.39:10) (בָּרֶקֶת), Eze.28:13 (יַהֲלֹם), etc. ;]
emerald or other trans parent green stone (LS, see word; DB, iv, 620; Swete, Ap., 67, 288): Rev.21:19.†
G4557:
σαρδόνυξ (L, σαρδιόνυξ), -υχος, ὁ
(σάρδιον, ὄνυξ),
sardonyx, a stone marked by the red of the sard and the white of the onyx: Rev.21:20.†
G5555:
χρυσό-λιθος, -ου, ὁ
[in LXX: Exo.28:20 36:20 (Exo.39:13), Eze.28:13 (תַּרְשִׁישׁ) * ;]
a chrysolite (on its identification, see Swete, Ap., 288 f.; DB, iv, 620): Rev.21:20.†
G0969:
βήρυλλος, -ου, ὁ, ἡ,
[in LXX: Tob.13:17 (-ύλλιον in Exo.28:20, שֹׁהַם * ;])
beryl, a jewel of sea-green colour: Rev.21:20.†
G5116:
τοπάζιον, -ου, τό
(and τόπαζος, ὁ), [in LXX: Exo.28:17 35:17 (Exo.39:10), Job.28:19, Eze.28:13 (פִּטְדָה), Psa.119:127 (פָּז)* ;]
topaz: Rev.21:20 (see Swete, in l).†
G5192:
ὑακίνθος, -ου, ό
[in LXX chiefly for תְּכֵלֶת ;]
hyacinth;
(a) in cl., a flower, prob. the dark blue iris;
(b) in late writers, a precious stone of the same colour, perhaps the sapphire: Rev.21:20 (Phil., FlJ, al.).†
G0271:
ἀμέθυστος, -ου, ἡ
(accusative to Plut., ἀ- μεθύω, being regarded as an antidote against drunkenness) [in LXX: Exo.28:19 36:19 39:12 Eze.28:13 * ;]
amethyst, a purple quartz: Rev.21:20.†
G4510:
ῥυπόω, -ῶ
(ῥύπος),
to make filthy: Rev.22:11 Rec. (AV, tr. as = ῥυπάω, to be filthy).†
G5333:
φαρμακός, -ή, -όν
[in LXX for כָּשַׁף, etc. ;]
devoted to magical arts. As subst., ὁ φ. = φαρμακεύς, a magician, sorcerer: Rev.21:8 22:15.†
